# Mission 14 attempt: a 33-point configuration with one convex heptagon

## Approach

I reproduced the classical 32-point Erdős–Szekeres lower-bound construction
using six deep-below clusters of sizes `1, 5, 10, 10, 5, 1`. An exact scan
confirmed that this starting set contains no convex 7-subset.

I then inserted a 33rd point and searched the cells of the arrangement of lines
determined by pairs of points. A move crosses one arrangement boundary at a
time. The search incrementally maintains, for every 7-subset, how many of its
4-subsets are non-convex; a 7-subset is convex exactly when that count is zero.
After insertion-only search reached one remaining convex heptagon, I allowed
all 33 points to move between adjacent cells and ran four independent
simulated-annealing searches.

The first ordinary `long double` run appeared to reach zero, but this was a
near-collinearity numerical artifact and failed after conversion to integer
coordinates. I therefore reran the search with GCC `__float128` geometry and
converted the result to integers by scaling the 40-decimal coordinates by
`10^40`.

## Result

The best exact integer configuration is in general position and has exactly
one convex 7-subset, with zero-based point indices:

```text
(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 32)
```

The mission verifier therefore reports `VALID score=0`, not score 1. Four
independent 100-bit simulated-annealing runs did not eliminate the last convex
heptagon.
